claim_or_recommendation: An RCD breaks a circuit when it detects an unbalanced or leaking current; modern consumer units have a main switch with fuses and/or circuit breakers, and older units may lack an RCD.
qualification: Supporting source only, no visible link (one visible Electrical Safety First link is the DIY page). Consumer-unit wording cross-checked on https://www.electricalsafetyfirst.org.uk/safety-advice/home-and-people/home-buyers/. Fuse/breaker sentence hedged with "generally"; ESF plugs-and-fuses page confirms a fuse blows when too much current is drawn through overload or fault (plug fuse context). No diagnosis of which device operates for which gate fault.

claim_or_recommendation: Circuit breakers tripping is a warning sign; get a registered electrician to check your electrics as soon as possible.
qualification: Verified wording in the FAQ on the DIY-ers page on 22 October. One visible ESF link. Applied as advice to call a professional, not as a gate-specific diagnosis.

claim_or_recommendation: Water ingress or damage to cabling, control boxes and connections may result in a risk of electric shock or failure to operate safely; powered gates should be installed and maintained by competent contractors.
qualification: Verified wording on HSE powered gates basics page. One visible HSE link. Listed areas are framed as possible areas for investigation, not parts to replace.

claim_or_recommendation: Gate work often needs different competencies, including electricians for wiring up and checking the basic safety of electrical components.
qualification: Supporting source only, no second visible HSE link. Paraphrased; no claim about which trade must attend first.

claim_or_recommendation: Part P (England) covers installations in a garden or on land associated with a dwelling where the supply comes from the dwelling. Notifiable: new circuit, consumer unit replacement, additions or alterations in special locations. Repairs, replacements and maintenance are not notifiable. Example 2.8b: connecting an electric gate to an existing isolator is not notifiable; a new circuit from the consumer unit to the isolator is.
qualification: Checked Approved Document P 2013 edition PDF (assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5a802da7ed915d74e622ceed/BR_PDF_AD_P_2013.pdf), requirement P1 scope (d), paragraphs 2.2, 2.5, 2.7 and 2.8b. England only; article says "In England" and the site is London. One visible gov.uk link (publication page).

claim_or_recommendation: A registered competent person self-certifies notifiable work, completes a BS 7671 electrical installation certificate and the Building Regulations compliance certificate goes to the occupier within 30 days.
qualification: Approved Document P paragraphs 3.3 and 3.4. Competent person scheme self-certification cross-checked on https://www.gov.uk/building-regulations-competent-person-schemes (supporting, not visibly linked).

claim_or_recommendation: BS 7671 is co-published by the IET and BSI; BS 7671:2018+A4:2026 is the current edition; the Amendment 2 transition period ended on 15 October 2026.
qualification: Verified wording on electrical.theiet.org/bs-7671/ on 22 October. One visible IET link. No claim that existing installations become unsafe or non-compliant because of the amendment.

claim_or_recommendation: Homeowner action limited to visual checks and one reset of the tripped device if nothing looks or smells wrong; leave it off if it trips again; no opening covers, consumer-unit fault-finding, disconnecting wires or bypassing protection.
qualification: Original safety framework set by the editorial brief. Stops at safe visual checks and a single reset; all further investigation referred to a qualified electrician or gate engineer. Forum fault-finding methods (removing neutrals, swapping breakers) explicitly discouraged.

claim_or_recommendation: Use the manual-release instructions supplied for the particular system; a released leaf can move; secure only as the instructions describe.
qualification: Consistent with existing /guides/how-to-manually-open-electric-gate/ guidance. No universal release procedure given.

claim_or_recommendation: Ask for findings, how the fault was confirmed, test records, attendance charge, investigation scope and approval of further work; no fixed price before diagnosis.
qualification: Original buyer guidance. No prices, ranges, response times, guarantees or unconfirmed services.

claim_or_recommendation: Tailored tripping-fault banner linking to unchanged same-page enquiry form.
qualification: Heading and description drafted for data/article-ctas.json route /blog/electric-gates-keep-tripping-electrics/. Get a Free Quote button unchanged, no topic fields or prefills, no free assessment or electrician attendance promised. Codex to review rendered banner; no test leads.
